findings.description: CON-SUP-103 permits a task to start at the limit and defines a late start as later than the limit. The requirement detects a fault when the task has not started within the limit, leaving the equality boundary ambiguous.
findings.requested_change: Define the detection condition so a start exactly at the configured limit is accepted and a later start is a fault.

findings.description: CON-SUP-103 permits execution up to the limit but calls execution longer than the limit an overrun detected at expiry. The requirement does not resolve how execution ending exactly at expiry is distinguished from an overrun.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the equality boundary and detection instant with the source owner, then specify an objectively distinguishable condition.

findings.description: The requirement refers to an allowed range but neither it nor CON-SUP-115 defines complete allowed values for configuration fields. CON-SUP-115 names a timing limit longer than the period, a zero period and an unknown task as out-of-range cases.
findings.requested_change: Specify or reference the allowed configuration values and identify the cases that must cause code 9; record unresolved limits as open points.

findings.description: The unconditional refresh at every control-cycle end conflicts with SYS-SUP-013, which prohibits refresh when a fault has been detected since the previous refresh, and with STK-SUP-005's healthy-task condition.
findings.requested_change: Qualify the scheduled refresh with the applicable health and fault conditions so the obligations are consistent.

findings.description: STK-SUP-005 permits watchdog servicing only while every supervised task is healthy. No detected fault since the previous refresh does not establish that every task is healthy, and may allow refresh after an earlier fault.
findings.requested_change: Specify the source-supported health condition for both watchdog refreshes and its relationship to detected and latched faults.

findings.description: The requirement says to verify program-code integrity but provides no reference value or method for deciding whether the check succeeds. OP-SYS-001 records that these are undecided.
findings.requested_change: After the source decision, specify or reference the integrity check and its acceptance criterion.

findings.description: The condition that the start-up program-code integrity check fails cannot be determined without the check method and reference value identified as undecided in OP-SYS-001.
findings.requested_change: After the source decision, reference an objectively defined failure criterion for the check.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 supplies the CRC-32 polynomial but not the other parameters needed to reproduce its value, such as initialization, reflection and final transformation. A matching stored value alone does not define a unique test.
findings.requested_change: Reference a complete CRC definition or record the missing parameters as an open point for a source decision.

findings.description: The requirement calls for a run-time code check but does not define how a segment is checked or judged intact. OP-SYS-001 records the missing method and reference value.
findings.requested_change: After the source decision, specify or reference the run-time integrity check and its acceptance criterion.

findings.description: The condition that a run-time segment check fails cannot be determined without the check method and reference value identified as undecided in OP-SYS-001.
findings.requested_change: After the source decision, reference an objectively defined failure criterion for the segment check.

findings.description: The unconditional reset request after entering the safe state also applies to a start-up configuration fault, whereas SYS-SUP-009 and CON-SUP-115 require that fault to latch the safe state. It also lacks an exception for the latch required by SYS-SUP-026.
findings.requested_change: Specify the reset behavior and its exceptions for latched safe-state conditions consistently with the source decisions.

findings.description: OP-SYS-002 records that CON-SUP-110 does not resolve when the latch applies relative to the third fault and third reset. The requirement repeats that ambiguity, preventing a consistent test sequence.
findings.requested_change: After the source decision, specify the exact event at which the latch takes effect.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 requires the latch and fault history to survive software and watchdog resets but not power loss. The requirement states only reset retention and omits the power-loss behavior.
findings.requested_change: Specify the source-required behavior of the latch and fault history on power loss.

findings.description: The unconditional high status after start-up checks pass conflicts with SYS-SUP-027, which requires the status signal to remain low while the safe state is latched. A software or watchdog reset need not clear that latch under CON-SUP-110.
findings.requested_change: Qualify the operational status transition to respect a retained safe-state latch and other applicable fault conditions.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 defines entities as task names, CODE or CONFIG, but does not determine the entity for watchdog-reset fault code 8. OP-SYS-003 records the missing decision, so a complete report for that fault cannot be judged.
findings.requested_change: After the source decision, specify the permitted entity for a watchdog-reset report.

findings.description: The response contains <state>, but neither the requirement nor CON-SUP-113 defines its permitted values or their meanings. OP-SYS-005 records the unresolved state vocabulary.
findings.requested_change: After the source decision, specify or reference the status values and their meanings.

findings.description: The instruction to return the last 8 fault reports does not define the response when fewer than eight reports exist, including immediately after a power-on with no retained history.
findings.requested_change: Specify the response for fewer than eight available reports, or record the missing behavior as an open point.

findings.description: CON-SUP-116 requires fault-injection hooks to exist only in test builds. The requirement requires them in test builds but does not prohibit their presence in other builds.
findings.requested_change: State the source-required restriction that the fault-injection hooks exist only in test builds.
